claim: By 23:59 Prague time on Monday 23 November 2026 the Czech government approves extending the regulation of petrol and diesel prices (maximum prices and capped retailer margins) beyond 30 November 2026.

runs.reason:
**Base rate.** The closest Czech precedents favor renewal, but the sample is small. The cabinet continued the spring fuel caps into May and renewed the autumn caps on October 26, six days before the November rules took effect. It also let the spring caps end on July 19 when market conditions improved. That makes another extension plausible, not automatic. ([ct24.ceskatelevize.cz](https://ct24.ceskatelevize.cz/clanek/domaci/vlada-projedna-zmeny-v-knihovnim-zakone-nebo-povinnosti-pro-dovozce-amalgamu-372824?utm_source=openai))

**What moves this forecast.** On November 13, Finance Minister Alena Schillerová said a decision was needed within a week to ten days, a timetable that points to November 23. On November 19, Prime Minister Andrej Babiš told reporters the cabinet had not considered the extension because Schillerová was absent, not because it had rejected it. Both facts favor a Monday decision. The Finance Ministry’s November 20 update still cited supply risks, which favors renewal, though its diesel ceiling had fallen to CZK 44.53 per litre from CZK 48.69 on October 26, weakening the case for keeping the caps. ([ceskenoviny.cz](https://www.ceskenoviny.cz/zpravy/2901670?utm_source=openai))

**Main reason for NO: timing.** The Government Office confirmed an 11:00 cabinet meeting on November 23, but its November 20 announcement did not mention fuel regulation, and I could not verify the full agenda. A deferral to November 30 would leave time to act before December 1 but would resolve this claim NO. I put the chance of a decision on the caps within the window at about 75%, and the chance of a qualifying extension given a decision at about 75%. A diesel excise extension alone does not count. ([vlada.gov.cz](https://vlada.gov.cz/cz/media-centrum/ocekavane-udalosti/23--listopadu-2026-schuze-vlady-cr-230251/?utm_source=openai))

The regulation in force is Government Decree No. 203/2026 Sb., which sets maximum petrol and diesel prices and a CZK 2.50/l retailer-margin cap only through 30 November 2026. The cabinet meets on Monday 23 November at 11:00, but the published ODok programme for that sitting does not contain a fuel-price item, and no December decree is in VeKLEP.

Base rate: this year’s two review points split. The spring regime was ended in late June once wholesale prices stabilised; the October regime was extended on Monday 26 October, five days before expiry, when the Finance Ministry said the oil-market shock had not eased. Same-day filing of the decree is a proven path.

Facts that move this case: Schillerová said on 13 November that a December decision was due within a week to ten days, so Monday is the outer edge of her own timetable. The 19 November sitting skipped the item only because she was in Brno. ČTK on 20 November said the cabinet might decide as early as Monday. The ministry’s page, updated 20 November, still cites Hormuz tanker and infrastructure risks even after Yanbu loadings resumed. Against extension, the caps themselves have fallen hard (petrol to 39.47 Kč/l, diesel to 44.53 Kč/l for 21–23 November), the diesel excise waiver costs about CZK 1.1 billion a month, and the refinery levy meant to offset it is still only in second reading.

Strongest reason the obvious “they will extend on Monday” reading fails: the criterion is not whether the caps survive past November, but whether an approving regulation or resolution is taken inside 22–23 November. Deferral to the Monday 30 November sitting, a mid-week meeting after the 26–27 November European Council, or a decision to let the decree lapse are all NO. Prices have already given the cabinet the same “stabilisation” cover it used in June, and nothing on the published agenda locks the item in for Monday.
